quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When you park on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: You must drive with extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign that forbids it.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn drivers about dangerous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. Follow them for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can lead to an accident.

questions.question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look toward the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you temporarily.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear next.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A yellow light tells you that a red light is coming next. Prepare to stop.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, position your car:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes to make your turn.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian signals with their hand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are breaking the law or being unsafe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It warns you that a barrier or island is ahead. Drive to the right of it.

questions.question: Who is most likely to be killed in a work zone accident?

options.text: Bicyclists
Workers and flaggers
Drivers and passengers
Motorcyclists

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers and passengers
questions.explanation: Drivers and passengers are killed most often in work zone accidents. Drive carefully in all construction areas.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a standard crossbuck sign. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Continue only after a flagger gives you permission, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are certain no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow all their instructions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are several curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are several curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has three or more curves.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, what is the minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) that is illegal?

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: It is illegal for drivers 21 or older to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Drive carefully and reduce your speed.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive carefully and slowly. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead, as they light up the road and objects better in foggy conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When a traffic signal turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
Accelerate as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A green light allows you to go through the intersection. However, you must first yield the right-of-way to any pedestrians or vehicles still in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you more.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter—only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. It makes your driving worse. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A defensive driver watches what other drivers are doing and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them more room in front of your car to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because other vehicles are unlikely to come.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If you are next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve. You cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no vehicles are coming.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to see your blind spot when passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder. Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, let that vehicle go first. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What types of drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these choices
questions.explanation: Many drugs can hurt your ability to drive. This includes illegal drugs, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug can be a crime.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the chance of a crash. If you drive faster than other cars, you will keep passing. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to talk to each other.
One driver can go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Usually, vehicles at a four-way stop go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to tell the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting a freeway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a freeway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and only enter when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only enter when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Failure to stop is against the law.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross dashed lines to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and enter at the same speed as the traffic around you. Always yield to other vehicles when entering a road.
